fixtures: evals/make_fixtures.py builds each repo on branch `feature` off `main`

evals.name: invoice-api-auth-injection
evals.prompt: I just added search, export and get-by-id endpoints to our invoice API on this branch. Can you do a security review of the change before I open the PR? It's multi-tenant, so orgs must never see each other's invoices.
evals.expected_output: Confirmed IDOR in get_invoice (no org_id check) and SQL injection via `q` in search_invoices; sort/export column allowlist and int(limit) recognised as safe lookalikes; scope and coverage stated.
assertions: Reports the cross-tenant IDOR in get_invoice (query by id without org_id) with file:line
Reports SQL injection via the `q` parameter in search_invoices with file:line
Does NOT report the allowlisted ORDER BY column in export_invoices or search_invoices as an injection finding
Each reported finding states attacker/preconditions, impact and a concrete fix
Severity and confidence are expressed separately; confidence is evidence-based (not a bare numeric score)
States the review scope (base/branch and files) and includes a not-covered/exclusions statement

evals.name: framer-unsafe-and-ci
evals.prompt: Review this branch of our frame-parsing crate for security problems. I made payload() faster with unsafe and added a PR auto-labelling workflow. Frames come from untrusted network peers.
evals.expected_output: Confirmed OOB read in payload() (length from peer, no bounds check); pull_request_target + checkout of PR head + write token + running PR-controlled script, and title interpolation into run:; tag() unsafe recognised as sound.
assertions: Reports the out-of-bounds read / unsound unsafe in payload() (peer-controlled length, no bounds check) with file:line
Does not dismiss the unsafe issue on the grounds that Rust is memory-safe
Reports that the pull_request_target workflow checks out and executes PR-head code (scripts/label.sh) with a write-scoped token/secrets
Reports script injection via ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }} interpolated into run:
Does NOT report tag()'s unsafe copy_nonoverlapping as a vulnerability
Does not exclude CI/workflow or shell issues as blanket out-of-scope

evals.name: devtool-safe-lookalikes
evals.prompt: security check on my branch pls — added a stats subcommand and a git clone step to our dev CLI, plus a small react component. anything exploitable?
evals.expected_output: No confirmed vulnerabilities: table allowlisted, subprocess list args with `--`, TOOL_CACHE env var is operator-controlled for a local dev CLI, JSX auto-escapes. Report says so plainly with coverage/assumptions, without inflating speculative issues.
assertions: Reports no High or Medium confirmed vulnerabilities
Does not flag the f-string SQL in stats() as injection (table is allowlisted)
Does not flag subprocess.run git clone as command injection
States assumptions (e.g. env var / CLI args are operator-controlled for a local dev tool) and what was not covered
